With that said, Loveland has logged 57 or more receiving yards and six or more catches three of the past four weeks and is clearly the Bears' go-to tight end in the passing game, so Roush's anticipated increase of offensive snaps doesn't necessarily make him a viable option in fantasy.

items.headline: Chicago signed Scott from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: Scott was elevated each of the past three weeks, so this was a necessary move for him to be eligible to continue suiting up on game days. The 27-year-old has been providing depth at running back in the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe), who has been sidelined for each of the three contests that Scott has been elevated. With that said, Scott has yet to log an offensive snap this season, so he's unlikely to be a factor on offense in Week 8 versus Seattle even if Monangai is absent again.

items.headline: Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 12 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
items.summary: With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out for a third straight game, Swift once again handled a workhorse role and parlayed it into some solid production. Swift's rushing yardage total was his third highest of the season, and the veteran back got into the end zone for the third straight game on a four-yard run late in the first quarter. He's up to seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but his touches will take a hit if Monangai is able to get healthy enough over the extended time between Thursday's game and a Week 8 road matchup against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2 to suit up for that contest.

items.headline: Walker went without a target while playing 10 of the Bears' 77 snaps on offense in Sunday's 31-23 win over the Falcons.
items.summary: Walker's afternoon came to an end just after the start of the fourth quarter, when he was ejected for headbutting a Falcons player at the end of a kickoff return. He was assessed his second 15-yard penalty of the day as a result, with his first coming on a roughing-the-kicker charge back in the third quarter. Walker will remain a key part of the Bears' special-teams units heading into a Week 7 matchup with the Patriots, but he's buried on the depth chart at receiver and isn't likely to see extended playing time on offense anytime soon.

items.headline: Gesicki caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Gesicki isn't seeing reliable volume in the form of targets, but he's been a big factor in the red zone this season, as he now has five touchdowns in six games. He's already one away from matching his career high, which was set in 2020 with the Dolphins. Gesicki is repping as the Bengals' slot receiver between Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but the latter two dominate the passing looks from Joe Burrow.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Grandy off the Vikings' practice squad Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Grandy spent the previous two seasons with Cincinnati prior to being a part of final cuts this past summer. With Tanner Hudson (pectoral) done for the season and Erick All going down with a knee injury Sunday against the Ravens, Grandy gives the Bengals another reliable tight end behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample.

items.headline: Higgins secured six of seven targets for 148 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
items.summary: The Bengals' air attack as a whole got off to a very sluggish start, leading to a scoreless first half. However, Cincinnati exploded for 35 points after intermission, and Higgins played a big role by posting team-high reception and receiving yardage totals while tying for the team lead in targets. The veteran wideout also recorded his second touchdown catch of the campaign on a 13-yard grab with just under five minutes remaining in the third quarter that gave Cincinnati a 14-13 lead. Higgins is averaging an outstanding 17.3 yards per reception on a 33-571-2 receiving line heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

items.headline: Meyers failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both fully healthy, Meyers played just 20 of 53 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on Joe Burrow's 32 dropbacks. Outside of his 7-82-0 receiving performance in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Meyers has totaled six catches for 59 yards in the other five games.

items.headline: Perine rushed four times for 16 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: The running back wasn't targeted in the passing game, but Perine notably subbed in for Chase Brown at the goal line to punch in a one-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter. It's become apparent that the coaches are trusting Perine more, and it's having an effect on Brown's production. Perine is up to 31 carries for 126 yards (4.1 YPC) and one touchdown through six games this season.

items.headline: Sample caught both of his targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Sample entered Week 7 with just five catches for 24 yards on six targets across five games, so he doubled his yardage total and secured his first touchdown with Sunday's performance. It goes without saying, but Sample isn't on the fantasy football radar.

items.headline: Young (knee) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.
items.summary: Young missed each of the Bengals' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a knee injury. The extra rest has paid dividends for the rookie fourth-rounder, who is on track to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown against the Ravens. He's operated in a minimal role offensively this season, having logged only two catches on as many targets for nine yards across three games.

items.headline: Hudson (pectoral) was placed on injured reserve by the Bengals on Monday.
items.summary: Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the team's 31-24 win over Miami in Week 5, so his transition to IR comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All will continue to operate as the team's primary options at tight end.

items.headline: Iosivas (thumb) is making good progress in his rehab, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
items.summary: Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Sept. 26 while recovering from a torn ligament in his left thumb that required surgery. The wide receiver is reportedly on track to be available to play in Week 10 against the Steelers, and he has an outside chance of returning one week prior against the Falcons in Spain on Nov. 8, per Petraglia.

items.headline: The Bengals placed Kattus (undisclosed) on their practice-squad injured list Tuesday.
items.summary: Kattus went undrafted in April and signed with Cincinnati as an undrafted free agent in early May. He didn't make the team's 53-man roster but was brought on to the practice squad Oct. 20. It's not clear what type of injury Kattus is dealing with, but now that he's on the injured list, he's not eligible to be elevated for the next four games.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Prieskorn to their practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Prieskorn has bounced around between several organizations' practice squads over the past two campaigns but has yet to be elevated for a regular-season game. Most recently, he spent time in Carolina's training camp before being cut in late August. Prieskorn's signing was one of a flurry of moves by Cincinnati involving tight ends Tuesday, as Erick All (knee) was placed on injured reserve, Josh Kattus (undisclosed) landed on the practice-squad injured list and Cam Grandy was signed to the active roster.

items.headline: Boston caught three of eight targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
items.summary: The wide receiver was the favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year after the first five weeks of the season, but he's now posted back-to-back subpar games against the Ravens and Titans. During those two contests, Boston has four catches for 42 yards on 13 targets. He's been extremely inefficient with his looks and isn't getting loose for big plays over the top of the defense. He'll try to get back on track next Sunday in Pittsburgh.

items.headline: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans.
items.summary: Estime carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in his 2026 debut during last week's win over the Ravens, but he'll be in street clothes Sunday while the Browns welcome Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Dylan Sampson (knee) back from injuries. So long as Judkins, Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin are all available for Cleveland, Estime could remain a fixture on the inactive list in the weeks to come.

items.headline: Fannin caught six of nine targets for 91 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
items.summary: The second-year tight end delivered a season high in receiving yards, and Fannin's last catch was his biggest. With the game tied at 24-24 in the final minute of the fourth quarter, Fannin took a short pass over the middle from Deshaun Watson and tacked on about 30 yards after the catch to set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. Fannin will take a 25-257-3 line on 39 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Steelers.

items.headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback Sunday against the Titans, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
items.summary: Dillon Gabriel (back) is staying on IR, so Green will once again serve as the emergency QB3 behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. As such, Green is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Watson and Sanders leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: McLaughlin turned five kickoff returns into 117 yards during the Browns' 27-24 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.summary: McLaughlin played a key role in the Browns' Week 6 win over the Ravens, when he had nine carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all four of his targets for 13 yards. However, his role on offense evaporated Sunday due to the returns of both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. McLaughlin figures to be limited to return duties moving forward unless one or both of Judkins or Sampson misses time.

items.headline: Sanders is active as the Browns' backup quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
items.summary: After Deshaun Watson had a listless performance in a blowout loss to the Jaguars in Week 1, Ian Rapoport of ESPN had reported that Sanders could get a chance to start as soon as Week 3 if the Browns continued to languish. Watson has since steadied the ship, leading the Browns to wins in four of their last five games to put them atop the AFC North standings heading into Week 7 action. As a result, Sanders doesn't appear likely to threaten Watson's standing atop the depth chart anytime soon, though Sanders will continue to suit up on game days ahead of rookie Taylen Green, who will once again be inactive Sunday as the Browns' emergency No. 3 quarterback.

items.headline: The Browns placed Means (knee) on the practice squad injured list Tuesday.
items.summary: Means appeared in seven regular-season games for the Saints in 2024. Since then, he's been trying to find a spot on an NFL roster, though injuries have been a significant barrier along the way. The 25-year-old is now ineligible to be elevated ahead of Cleveland's next four regular-season games.

items.headline: The Browns signed Ryan to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The Browns waived Ryan from the active roster Monday. The tight end cleared waivers and was promptly invited back to the team as part of the 16-man practice squad. Ryan has played in six regular-season games for the Browns this year and has accumulated 73 special-teams snaps and two offensive snaps with no box-score output.

items.headline: Ferguson failed to haul in his lone target during Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: Monday was the first time since Week 8 of the 2025 season that Ferguson failed to record a catch, and the only pass he saw from Dak Prescott was on a broken play in the red zone early in the fourth quarter. Ferguson's 38 offensive snaps were only two more than fellow tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford, and the latter's role in the offense has grown over the last few weeks at the expense of the former. Week 8 against the Cardinals presents itself as a bounce-back opportunity for Ferguson, seeing as Arizona's defense ranks 27th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to tight ends.

items.headline: Goodson turned 10 carries into 38 yards and returned two kickoffs for 42 yards during the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday.
items.summary: The Cowboys relied heavily on the run game Monday, and Goodson saw a season-high 10 rushes as a result, although that was still well behind the workload of lead back Javonte Williams, who turned 25 carries into a career-high 155 yards and a score. Goodson nearly found the end zone himself after returning a 91-yard kickoff to the house in the second quarter, only for the touchdown to be nullified by a holding penalty on Dallas. He's limited to RB2 duties for the time being but would step into an elevated role if Williams were to ever miss time. The Cowboys will head back home for Week 8 against the Cardinals, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (126.4).

items.headline: Schoonmaker went without a target while playing 11 of the Cowboys' 68 offensive snaps in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: After drawing even with Brevyn Spann-Ford in snaps during the Cowboys' Week 1 loss to the Giants, Schoonmaker has settled in as the clear No. 3 option on the depth chart at tight end behind Jake Ferguson and Spann-Ford in the subsequent six games. He's played less than 20 percent of the offensive snaps in four consecutive contests, drawing just one target during that span while functioning mainly as a blocker during his time on the field.

items.headline: Spann-Ford finished with two catches for 11 yards on two targets in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
items.summary: With the Cowboys opening the game in 12 personnel, Spann-Ford was credited with a start and was on the field for 36 of the team's 68 offensive snaps on the night (52.9 percent). Though Jake Ferguson is locked in as Dallas' top tight end, Spann-Ford has consistently repped ahead of Luke Schoonmaker as the No. 2 option at the position since Week 2. While he's mainly functioned as a blocker, Spann-Ford has been a solid complementary option in the passing game with a 9-79-0 line on 13 targets.

items.headline: Williams rushed 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.summary: Williams broke out for a new single-game career high in rushing yards during the impressive victory, sealing the win with a two-yard scoring run just ahead of the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The remarkable performance also marked Williams' first 100-yard tally of the season, and he's been highly rewarding for fantasy managers by scoring a touchdown in five straight games. Williams should have a prime opportunity to continue building on his strong first half of the season in Week 8, as he'll face a vulnerable Cardinals run defense at home on Sunday.

items.headline: The Cowboys signed Trask to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Trask is best known for his time with the Buccaneers. In seven regular-season appearances with Tampa Bay, the 2021 No. 64 overall pick attempted only 11 passes, completing four of them. Trask is seemingly a long way from being active for an NFL game and may only see the field as an emergency quarterback. That likely won't change as long as Dak Prescott and Sam Howell are available.

items.headline: Dobbins and Jonah Coleman will lead the Broncos' backfield against the Chiefs on Sunday due to the absence of RJ Harvey (knee), Eric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.summary: Harvey popped up on Thursday's injury report due to a knee injury and was unable to practice Friday, which resulted in him being ruled out for Sunday's AFC West tilt. Dobbins found the end zone in Week 7 against the Cardinals but was less efficient with his carries than Coleman, although the duo could have a fairly even split in backfield duties in Harvey's absence. Through seven regular-season games. Dobbins has turned 87 carries into 293 yards (3.4 YPC) and three touchdowns while adding eight catches on nine targets for 27 yards.

items.headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.summary: Ehlinger will only be available if quarterbacks Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Engram caught one of three targets for two yards during Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Engram played a season-low 23 offensive snaps in the victory, and as a result, he was limited to one or zero catches for the fourth time this season. The tight end hasn't reached the end zone since Week 1, and he'll remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Chiefs.

items.headline: Franklin failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Franklin played 28 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. Despite being on the field for 46 percent of the Broncos' offensive plays, the No. 3 option was targeted only twice and failed to catch either pass.

items.headline: Harvey (knee) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, but his injury isn't considered severe or long term, Sam Jane of The Denver Post reports.
items.summary: Harvey was a mid-week addition to the injury report, listed as limited Thursday and absent Friday. It sounds like he may only miss a game or two, but that could impact his role down the stretch if rookie Jonah Coleman takes advantage of the opportunity ahead. Coleman took half of the snaps and half of the backfield opportunities last week in his first game back from injured reserve, while Harvey was limited to a 25 percent snap share and five touches, relying on a 52-yard TD reception to salvage his fantasy day. Harvey's absence could free up a few more snaps and touches for Coleman or J.K. Dobbins.

items.headline: Mims (ankle) practiced fully Thursday,Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.summary: Mims was a limited participant in Wednesday's session, but the wideout's full participation a day later sets the stage for him to be available Sunday against the Chiefs. The 2023 second-rounder has two catches in each of his last three games, with his Week 8 fantasy upside linked to the status of top WR Jaylen Waddle, who is managing a chest injury.

items.headline: Waddle (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs after he was a limited participant in Friday's practice.
items.summary: After opening the week with a missed practice and then logging limited sessions Thursday and Friday, Waddle's status remains unsettled heading into the weekend. The Broncos and Chiefs are scheduled for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, which could mean limited alternatives for fantasy managers if Waddle comes down to a game-time decision and then doesn't play. If that were to happen, Denver would likely look to Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey to take more WR snaps alongside Courtland Sutton.

items.headline: The Broncos placed Badie (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Per Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette, Badie broke his thumb during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. Badie is required to miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move, and if he's cleared to play Sunday, then he would slot in as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

items.headline: Pancol signed with Denver's practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Pancol was cut from Indianapolis' practice squad last week, but it didn't take long to find a new squad. The Duke product has yet to log any NFL regular-season action since originally signing as an undrafted free agent with Jacksonville in April of 2025. Pancol will provide tight-end depth for the Broncos, though he's unlikely to be elevated in the near future given that Denver currently has four healthy tight ends on its roster.

items.headline: The Lions signed Carter to the active roster Thursday.
items.summary: Carter last played for Cleveland in 2025, and he served as the team's main return man. The 33-year-old veteran is expected to do the same for Detroit after the season-ending knee injury to Tom Kennedy, per Eric Woodyard of ESPN.com.

items.headline: St. Brown (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
items.summary: Head coach Dan Campbell told Richard Silva of The Detroit News on Monday that St. Brown tweaked his ankle during this past Sunday's win against the Packers, and while the wide receiver sat out Wednesday's session, he was able to handle a full workload one day later, fulfilling Campbell's prediction. St. Brown thus should be good for the 11.3 targets per game that he's averaged through six appearances this season Sunday versus the Vikings.

items.headline: TeSlaa caught one of his two targets for 10 yards in the Lions' 20-17 win over the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: TeSlaa played 33 offensive snaps for the Lions in the contest, a 49 percent share of Detroit's offensive plays. However, TeSlaa saw a mere two targets for the second straight game after logging a season-high eight against the Panthers in Week 4, and Sunday's catch was his first since that game as well.

items.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Pacheco (back) has a chance to return in late December, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
items.summary: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

items.headline: Golden brought in seven of 13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
items.summary: The second-year speedster finished second in receptions and receiving yards for the Packers on the night, while also leading the way in targets with a season-high-tying figure. Golden struck for his fourth touchdown of the season as well on a 24-yard scoring grab just after the two-minute warning in the first half, and the 2025 first-round pick now has at least six catches in four consecutive contests. He should remain busy in a Week 9 road showdown against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8, one where New England shutdown cornerback Christian Gonzalez could spend the majority of his time on Christian Watson.

items.headline: Johnson (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Panthers, Mike Spofford of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Johnson didn't suit up in the Week 7 loss to Detroit. The 23-year-old will be held out for a second consecutive contest, and he likely won't get back on the field moving forward if Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd and Pierre Strong are active.

items.headline: Lloyd rushed three times for seven yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
items.summary: In his second game of the season, Josh Jacobs logged a total of 27 touches, leaving precious little work for any other back. Lloyd slightly outpaced Pierre Strong by two carries, but he still logged a season low in rush attempts. With Jacobs looking fully capable of handling a workhorse role moving forward, Lloyd may be destined for similar volume to Thursday's on most weeks as long as his star teammate is available.

items.headline: Melton caught one of his two targets for four yards and logged a 24-yard kickoff return in the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Melton played 13 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver remains a versatile depth option for the Packers, filling in wherever he is needed without garnering much attention.

items.headline: The Packers signed Owen from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: Owen was elevated for the Packers' Week 6 win over the Cowboys. The wide receiver played just three snaps on special teams in the contest and has likely earned a roster spot as a depth option while Skyy Moore (ankle) and Jayden Reed (neck) are on IR. Owen could be involved in the return game against the Lions on Sunday.

items.headline: Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Panthers Mike Spofford of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Smith has appeared in each of the Packers' seven regular-season games. However, he will be a healthy scratch Thursday night, meaning Mark Redman and Josh Whyle will be behind Tucker Kraft on the depth chart.

items.headline: Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in Sunday night's 23-13 win over the Cowboys. He caught five of six targets for 39 yards.
items.summary: Strong led the backfield in carries and out-targeted MarShawn Lloyd six to one. The Packers still couldn't run the ball effectively, but Josh Jacobs is due back from the Commissioner's Exempt list in time for next Sunday's game against the Lions, making all three of Strong, Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson waiver-wire material in fantasy moving forward. Strong has turned 16 carries into just 35 yards through two games, but he's secured eight of 10 targets for 50 yards.

items.headline: Williams caught three passes on as many targets for 47 yards and turned two carries into four yards during the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Quarterback Jordan Love spread the ball around Sunday to eight different receivers, and Williams was one of five pass catchers to record at least three receptions. Williams finished fourth on the team in receiving yards, with two of his catches going for 27 and 20 yards in the first and second quarters, respectively. The second-year pro is cemented as the Packers' WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and tight end Tucker Kraft also is in the mix for looks from Love. The Packers will head back to Lambeau Field and practice on a short week for Thursday night's game against the Panthers, whose defense ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (195.7) and fifth in passing touchdowns allowed (seven).

items.headline: The Packers placed Moore (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Moore wasn't able to return after injuring his ankle last Sunday against the Bears, and in the midst of not practicing during Week 6 prep, he was seen wearing a boot on his left boot and using a scooter to move about the locker room, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Moore thus will miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Nov. 15 against the Vikings. In Moore's absence, some combination of Bo Melton, Savion Williams (ankle) and Matthew Golden likely will handle return duties.

items.headline: Packers head coach Matt Lafleur said Thursday it's "tough to say" whether Musgrave (neck) plays this season, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
items.summary: Musgrave has yet to return to the Packers since being placed on the PUP list prior to Week 1 of the regular season, and until the 26-year-old proves otherwise, he will likely continue to sit out. Tucker Kraft and Jonnu Smith will continue leading the charge at the tight end position.

items.headline: Boutte caught one of two targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss versus the Giants.
items.summary: Boutte played a season-low 18 offensive snaps in Week 7, trailing behind Nico Collins (34) and Xavier Hutchinson (31) and tying with Jaylin Noel (toe). Predictably, Boutte wasn't very involved in an inefficient passing game. As recent trade acquisition Marvin Harrison gets acclimated, Boutte's role probably will continue to shrink as the campaign continues.

items.headline: Collins caught two of five targets for six yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Collins was surprisingly quiet as C.J. Stroud spread the ball out to nine different targets, including six wide receivers. Collins remains atop the wide-receiver depth chart and hadn't dipped below 55 receiving yards in a regular-season appearance since Week 7 of last season. The star wideout's recent track record suggests Collins will likely bounce back in Week 9 against the Chargers following Houston's Week 8 bye.

items.headline: Hutchinson caught three of six targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants. He added 12 rushing yards on two attempts.
items.summary: On a day in which C.J. Stroud targeted nine different players, Hutchinson tied Dalton Schultz for the team lead with six targets. Nico Collins led the wideout group with 24 routes, but Hutchinson tied Jaylin Noel (toe) for second at the position with 15 routes. In a receiver room that is running six deep on game days, none of these Houston wide receivers are reliably playable in fantasy outside of Collins.

items.headline: Jordan (foot) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.summary: Jordan likely sustained his foot injury during Thursday's practice, but the tight end was quickly able to upgrade to a full participant in Friday's practice. Jordan is all set to suit up as a depth option at tight end in Sunday's contest.

items.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said that Jordan was placed  on the practice squad injured list Wednesday due to a quadriceps injury, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: With David Montgomery (groin) sidelined this past Sunday against the Jaguars in London, Jordan was elevated from the practice squad and made his season debut, working as the No. 2 back behind Woody Marks. Jordan took advantage of the opportunity, recording six carries for 43 yards and one touchdown and hauling in his only target for seven yards. Now that he's on the practice squad injured list, however, he must miss at least the next four games, meaning he won't be eligible to play again until Nov. 29 against the Ravens.

items.headline: Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Mark remained busy in the absence of David Montgomery (groin), handling 20 touches while no other running back got a touch for the Texans. Over the last three games, the first of which Montgomery left early and the last two of which he missed, Marks has recorded 247 scrimmage yards on 56 touches. Marks missed some action in the second half Sunday due to a leg injury but returned to the game. Houston's Week 8 bye will give both Marks and Montgomery a chance to heal up, and Houston would likely return to a backfield platoon in Week 9 against the Chargers if Montgomery's ready to play.

items.headline: Montgomery (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.summary: Montgomery still hasn't returned to practice and will miss a second straight game, leaving Woody Marks to handle a large workload against the Giants. Jawhar Jordan (quad) was effective off the bench last week, but he's now on the practice-squad injured list, which leaves Dare Ogunbowale as the No. 2 RB. Ogunbowale's history as a special teamer and passing-down specialist suggest Marks should dominate carries.

items.headline: Moreau played 21 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in the Texans' 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.summary: Moreau did not appear in the box score of Sunday's game. The tight end's complete lack of offensive production was in stark contrast to his Week 6 two-touchdown effort against the Jaguars in London, and Moreau's week-to-week production figures to remain erratic while working behind clear No. 1 option Dalton Schultz.

items.headline: Ogunbowale didn't record an offensive touch or target in Sunday's 24-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Even with David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured and inactive, Ogunbowale played just seven offensive snaps behind Woody Marks' 54. Ogunbowale can continue to be ignored in fantasy football.

items.headline: Schultz caught five of six targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: The veteran tight end paced the Texans with his six targets, matching Xavier Hutchinson, as the duo saw one more than Nico Collins on a day when C.J. Stroud targeted nine different pass catchers. Schultz is still looking for his first touchdown of the season and has settled in as a low-ceiling fantasy tight end.

items.headline: Alie-Cox failed to haul in either of his targets during the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Alie-Cox led all Colts tight ends with 39 offensive snaps, but he could not connect with Daniel Jones on two pass attempts from the veteran quarterback. Alie-Cox and the other Indianapolis tight ends were operating in elevated roles for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). Alie-Cox's snap count would take a hit if Warren was cleared to return for Week 8 against Jacksonville.

items.headline: Allen caught all three of his targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: Allen was held to his fewest catches, receiving yards and targets since Week 2 as the Colts struggled to establish a passing attack against Minnesota's impressive defense. The wide receiver still led the team in all three categories, and he'll have a chance for better production in Week 8 versus the Jaguars.

items.headline: Dulin (hamstring) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
items.summary: That's two straight limited sessions to begin the week for Dulin after he missed the Colts' past two games due to a hamstring issue. The veteran wideout appears to be making progress in his recovery, as he didn't practice at all during Week 5 and Week 6 prep. Dulin's likelihood of returning for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota should gain clarity with the release of Friday's injury report and game designations.

items.headline: Giddens did not play a single snap during Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: Giddens dressed for Sunday's game, but he observed the entire contest from the sidelines while Seth McGowan served as the Colts' lone backup to Jonathan Taylor. Giddens has yet to play a snap this regular season, but that could change if the Colts -- who have a 2-5 record -- are sellers at the trade deadline and opt to send Taylor to another team.

items.headline: Gould (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 8 tilt against Jacksonville.
items.summary: Gould suffered a concussion Week 6 against Tennessee and didn't play last Sunday versus Minnesota. Though he logged full practice sessions both Thursday and Friday this week, it appears he hasn't yet been cleared to suit up by an independent neurologist. As such, Gould will have to sit out another contest, which will primarily impact Indianapolis' plans for the return game.

items.headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Leonard will continue to serve as the team's emergency QB3, and as such, he is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Mallory did not catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota.
items.summary: Mallory and the other Colts tight ends worked in larger roles offensively Sunday due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). However, the former's 21 offensive snaps ranked third behind Mo Alie-Cox (39) and Drew Ogletree (35), and Mallory could not connect with Daniel Jones, with the third and final pass that came his way resulting in an interception by Harrison Smith. Mallory has seen nine targets over his last two games since coming off injured reserve, but his role would shrink against the Jaguars in Week 8 if Warren is given the green light to play in that contest.

items.headline: Ogletree (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.summary: Ogletree's practice reps Wednesday and Thursday were limited by a knee injury that he likely picked up against the Vikings in Week 7. He was a DNP for Friday's session, but the Colts have left the door open for Ogletree to suit up Sunday, depending on how his knee feels over the weekend and during pregame warmups. Tyler Warren (groin) has been cleared to return from a two-game absence, but Ogletree's absence would mean more offensive snaps would be available for Will Mallory, Mo Alie-Cox and Pharaoh Brown.

items.headline: Treadwell caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
items.summary: Treadwell played 45 offensive snaps in Sunday's loss. The wide receiver participated in 74 percent of the Colts' offensive plays, but the No. 3 option saw fewer targets than Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

items.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) will "most likely not" have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 8, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
items.summary: A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

items.headline: The Colts signed Hardman to the practice squad Tuesday,
items.summary: Hardman spent time with the Bills during training camp but was released ahead of the 2026 campaign. The veteran will get a chance to continue his NFL career with the Colts, and his services on special teams could be needed sooner rather than later if Ashton Dulin (hamstring) and Anthony Gould (concussion) can't suit up for the Week 7 meeting with the Vikings.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.summary: Allen popped up on Thursday's injury report due to a hamstring injury, but despite logging back-to-back limited practices to end Week 8 prep, the second-year running back has been cleared to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt. He has only one carry through six regular-season games while operating as the team's RB3 behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez.

items.headline: Boerkircher caught both of his targets for eight yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: Boerkircher was able to find pay dirt for the first time in his NFL career, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter. The 25-year-old now has gathered in six of eight targets for 52 yards and a touchdown over six contests to open the regular season.

items.headline: Cameron didn't garner a target and recorded 46 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: Cameron went without a target for the first time since Week 2, but he did play a season-high 50 percent of the team's offensive snaps. The wide receiver played 19 more snaps on offense than Brian Thomas, and he appears to have officially taken over as the team's No. 3 option behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers at his position. On the year, Cameron has caught eight of 12 targets for 117 yards and two touchdowns while also adding 245 yards as a kick returner over six games.

items.headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.summary: Meyers didn't practice Friday, but the Jaguars are leaving the light on for the veteran wideout to face Indianapolis. He's coming off a productive Week 6 game against the Texans in which Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards. The Jaguars are fresh off their bye. If Meyers can't go, Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would have expanded roles behind Parker Washington.

items.headline: Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards while failing to reel in his only target during Sunday's 34-31 loss to Houston.
items.summary: Rodriguez led the team in rushing yards, out-producing fellow running back Bhayshul Tuten's 39 yards on 12 carries. Although the two split the carries almost evenly, Tuten caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two scores in the contest. Rodriguez has now compiled 168 yards on 39 carries while catching one pass for six yards over six contests to open the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Strange caught five of seven targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: Strange finished tied for the team lead in catches with wide receiver Jakobi Meyers, while his seven targets were third behind Meyers (10) and Parker Washington (11). The tight end has now reeled in at least five passes in three straight contests, compiling 207 receiving yards on 19 catches in those games. The Jaguars are off in Week 7, so his next chance to continue his momentum will come Nov. 1 against the Colts.

items.headline: Washington caught four of 11 targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: Despite leading the Jaguars in targets, Washington finished second to Jakobi Meyers in both catches and receiving yards, and he wasn't on the other end of any of Trevor Lawrence's four TDs. It's the third time in the last four games that Washington has failed to reach five grabs or 70 yards, but the fourth contest featured a 6-124-2 line from the fourth-year wideout. Washington will take a 26-416-4 line on 46 targets into a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

items.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday that Allen will "get a little bit more [snaps]" during Sunday's game against the Broncos, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: While the Chiefs have been without top wideout Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) in the past two games, Allen has seen only a modest uptick in playing time. After logging no more than five offensive snaps in each of his first four NFL contests, Allen has played 25 total offensive snaps over the last two weeks while recording three receptions for 45 yards. Even if Reid sticks to his promise to find more work for Allen, it's unclear how much larger his role would grow if Rice is able to put an end to his absence this weekend. Rice took a step in the right direction toward playing in Denver by returning to the practice field Wednesday, per Taylor.

items.headline: Armstrong caught one of two targets for three yards during Sunday night's 20-3 loss to Seattle.
items.summary: Armstrong was signed to the active roster ahead of Week 7, and he was on the field for 56 percent of the team's offensive snaps. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) still banged up, it's possible that Armstrong operates in a similar role in Week 8 versus Denver.

items.headline: Gray caught three passes on as many targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Gray and Travis Kelce ended up tied for the most receiving yards on the Chiefs on Sunday, although the offense struggled as a whole, with Patrick Mahomes throwing for only 165 yards and Kenneth Walker averaging only 2.6 yards per carry. Gray has caught 11 of 12 passes for 153 yards over his last four games, though he's limited to a complementary role in the passing game behind Kelce, Xavier Worthy and, when healthy, Rashee Rice (knee/hamstring). The Chiefs will stay on the road for Week 8 against the Broncos, whose defense ranks 24th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to tight ends.

items.headline: Johnson caught two of three passes for 17 yards and returned three kickoffs for 81 yards during Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. He also added two tackles on special teams.
items.summary: Johnson was held without a carry for the second time in three games, with lead back Kenneth Walker bottled up for 36 yards on 14 carries (2.6 YPC). Johnson has seen three carries or fewer in four of the first six games of the regular season and figures to be limited to a third-down role as a pass catcher unless Walker misses time. The Chiefs will stay on the road for a Week 8 divisional matchup against the Broncos on Nov. 1.

items.headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's game against the Seahawks.
items.summary: The rookie seventh-round pick continues to sit behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields to begin the season.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Ott from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: The Chiefs placed Brashard Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday in a corresponding move. Smith's injury leaves an opportunity for Ott. The undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma could make his NFL debut during Sunday Night Football as the Chiefs take on the Seahawks in Week 7.

items.headline: Royals caught two of his four targets for 24 yards during Kansas City's win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.summary: Royals saw increased playing time with Rashee Rice out due to a hamstring injury and ended up amassing a season-high 24 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick has now caught five passes for 41 yards and a touchdown across five games this season and could once again serve as the team's No. 2 receiver should Rice remain sidelined for the Week 7 matchup against the Seahawks.

items.headline: Watson reverted to the Chiefs' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Watson was elevated to the active roster for a second week in a row ahead of Sunday night's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. The wide receiver reeled in his only target for seven yards while playing five snaps on offense and two snaps with the special-teams unit. The Chiefs can elevate Watson one more time before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

items.headline: The Chiefs placed Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Smith sustained a hamstring injury in Thursday's practice session and has promptly been transitioned to IR as he manages the issue. Running back Jaydn Ott has been signed to the active roster to be the No. 3 option behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson while Smith recovers.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Carter to the practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Carter was cut from the Chiefs' practice squad Wednesday, but he's back in his old spot just two days later. He has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026 after in appearing in nine contests for the Falcons in 2025.

items.headline: Bowers (calf) was a full practice participant Thursday.
items.summary: Bowers opened Week 8 prep with a limited session Wednesday due to a calf injury, but it didn't deter him from returning to all drills one day later. Since making his season debut in Week 3, he's gone for more than 70 receiving yards in all five of his appearances, sitting on a 34-455-3 line on 52 targets on the campaign.

items.headline: Mayer caught all three targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: After a big Week 6 in which Mayer caught seven of nine targets for 95 yards against the Bills, Mayer faded into the background against Los Angeles, as Tre Tucker (5-103-1 receiving), Brock Bowers (6-73-0) and Ashton Jeanty (8-61-1) accounted for most of the production in the passing game for the Raiders. Mayer will be a fantasy TE1/2 for next Sunday's game against the Jets.

items.headline: The Raiders cut Myarick from the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Myarick was elevated for two games this season, logging eight offensive snaps and three special-teams snaps without registering any stats. The tight end remains a free agent able to sign with any franchise's active roster or practice squad.

items.headline: Nailor caught two of five targets for 14 yards during Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Nailor was able to reel in multiple passes for the first time since Week 1, but he was still limited to an uninspiring 14 receiving yards. With Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty combining for 28 targets in the contest, Nailor operated as the No. 4 option at best for Las Vegas. Through six contests this year, the wide receiver has caught eight of 20 targets for 75 yards, and he is still searching for his first touchdown.

items.headline: O'Connell (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Raiders' emergency third quarterback against the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: O'Connell will only enter Sunday's game if both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza must exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Thomas (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Thomas was a full participant in Friday's practice, which was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Sunday's road tilt. He has five catches on as many targets for 60 yards and one touchdown through seven regular-season games and will continue to serve as the Raiders' TE3 behind Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer.

items.headline: The Raiders reinstated Thornton (hamstring) from injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: With Thornton's 21-day practice window coming to a close this week, the Raiders elected to move him back on to the 53-man roster. A full participant in each of the Raiders' last nine practices, Thornton looks like he'll be ready to play this Sunday against the Jets, but he may not be in store for a meaningful role in the receiver rotation. He struggled to carve out consistent volume in the passing game as a rookie fourth-round pick in 2025, putting together a 10-135-0 receiving line on 30 targets over 15 appearances.

items.headline: Tucker secured five of 12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: Tucker led the Raiders in receiving yards and targets on the afternoon with a big lift from a game-long 41-yard catch and a 37-yard fourth-quarter touchdown reception. The speedy wideout has a combined 10-200-3 line over his last two games alone as he continues to take his chemistry with Kirk Cousins to new levels, and Tucker is averaging a stellar 16.3 yards per reception heading into a favorable Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

items.headline: Washington rushed six times for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Despite dealing with foot and back injuries throughout the practice week, Washington played against Los Angeles and handled his normal workload behind starter Ashton Jeanty. Even though Jeanty again handled more carries, Washington ended up leading the team in rushing yards on a day the Raiders ran for just 48 yards. Washington is pushing Jeanty for more rushing work, but it's not enough at this point to warrant starting the rookie running back in fantasy.

items.headline: White caught one of three targets for four yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: White has now posted back-to-back duds, totaling one catch for four yards on five targets across the last two contests. In an offense that doesn't often use three wide receivers on the field at once, White is pretty clearly behind both Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor for snaps and routes. White ran just nine routes on Kirk Cousins' 48 dropbacks in Week 7.

items.headline: Bech (forearm) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Bech was a full practice participant Wednesday through Friday, so it won't come as any surprise if he's activated from injured reserve before the 4 p.m. ET deadline Saturday (to be eligible for Sunday's game). He opened the year as the Raiders' No. 2 wide receiver, but minimal production from Jalen Nailor could open an opportunity to climb the depth chart in November/December.

items.headline: Runyon (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Like Week 7 prep, Runyon was a full participant in all three practice sessions for Week 8. However, the Towson product is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve as he continues to recover from a foot injury. Runyon's 21-day practice window opened Oct. 14, so he would be forced to stay on IR for the rest of the season if he's not activated by this upcoming Wednesday.

items.headline: The Raiders cut Scott (undisclosed) from the practice squad injured list Wednesday.
items.summary: Scott will hit the open market and will have the opportunity to sign with a team once he's fully healthy. He has not appeared in a regular-season game since 2024 as a member of the Bears.

items.headline: Harris (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.
items.summary: Harris, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston have all missed time this season, but they're healthy after a Week 7 bye. Prior to the team's onslaught of injuries, Harris actually saw more targets (21) than Johnston (19) over the first four weeks of the season.

items.headline: Herbert completed 22 of 37 passes for 204 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed five times for 26 yards.
items.summary: Herbert continued to struggle but once again got little help from his teammates. Top wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) exited early, and the Chargers couldn't generate much on the ground, as Herbert led the team in rushing yards. Herbert was held without a touchdown for the first time this season after throwing exactly one touchdown pass in each of the previous five games. The 0-6 Chargers are the first team to six losses this season, as the Titans notched their first win of the season over the Colts on Sunday to improve to 1-5, while the winless Dolphins were on bye. Herbert will be on bye in Week 7 before his next opportunity to snap this season-opening losing streak in a nominal road game against the Rams in Week 8.

items.headline: Johnston's role in the passing game will shrink slightly in Week 8 against the Rams given that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) have been cleared to play, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
items.summary: Both Johnston and McConkey were sidelined for Week 5, but the latter entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 6 loss to the Chiefs. Johnston logged 17 targets through his first three games of the regular season, although he's seen only five passes from Justin Herbert over his last two outings, which Johnston turned into two catches for 101 yards. The Chargers are averaging only 168.2 passing yards per game this season -- which ranks 28th in the NFL -- and they face a Rams defense that boasts the fourth-best pass defense in the league (186.3 passing yards allowed per game).

items.headline: Kolar caught three of six targets for 20 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
items.summary: Kolar finished fifth on the Chargers in receiving yards, but he was also second on the team in both catches and targets behind KeAndre Lambert-Smith (five catches on nine targets for 32 yards). Kolar has a 6-57-0 receiving line in his two outings since returning from a two-game absence due to a fractured forearm, but he's stuck in an offense that is one of the worst units in the league this season. The Chargers will look to regroup during the Week 7 bye before facing the Rams in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Lambert-Smith is likely to drop down the wideout pecking order Sunday versus the Rams, as Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) are set to return to action.
items.summary: McConkey missed most of Week 6, and Harris sat out that contest altogether. As a result, Lambert-Smith logged an 87 percent offensive snap share, which he turned into his first five catches and 39 yards of the season on nine targets. However, the Chargers' bye week has provided enough time for McConkey and Harris to recover, so Lambert-Smith will probably go back to a very minor role on offense.

items.headline: Mitchell turned two carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned four kickoffs for 87 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Week 6 was the lowest usage Mitchell has seen this season, and his 17 snaps on offense were third most among Chargers running backs behind Omarion Hampton (34) and Kimani Vidal (25). Through six regular-season games, Mitchell has turned 35 carries into 139 yards and added 12 catches (on 15 targets) for 52 yards and a score, but it's hard to put much trust into any of the Chargers' skill-position players given the team's poor start to the season. Perhaps the Week 7 bye will help the Chargers right the ship, with their next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
items.summary: Thompson didn't play a snap in Week 6 against the Chiefs despite being active for the contest due to a lingering quadriceps injury. He'll be inactive for Sunday's game, so KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Theo Wease and Derius Davis are all candidates for a bump in offensive snaps. Thompson's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Texans on Sunday, Nov. 8.

items.headline: Vidal turned seven carries into 21 yards and caught three of four passes for 19 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
items.summary: The Chargers' run offense struggled Sunday, but Vidal was slightly more efficient than Omarion Hampton (18 yards) on the same number of carries. Vidal has seen more rotational offensive snaps over the Chargers' last three games, and over that span he has logged 20 carries for 103 yards and a touchdown and six catches (on nine targets) for 29 yards and a score. His role may continue to expand following the Week 7 bye, with the Chargers' next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: The Chargers signed Palmer to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Palmer spent a brief amount of time with both the Patriots and Cardinals during training camp, but he's been without a team until Tuesday. He's appeared in only one regular-season game since entering the league as a sixth-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2024 NFL Draft. The Chargers face the Rams on Sunday, and Palmer could be a candidate for elevation to the active roster depending on the statuses of fellow wide receivers Ladd McConkey (concussion), Tre' Harris (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps).

items.headline: Atwell wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: With Davante Adams (hamstring) out, Atwell was active and played 25 offensive snaps. He ran 20 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks, tying Konata Mumpfield for second on the team behind Puka Nacua's 31, but Atwell was just doing cardio out there. He's not a reliable fantasy target, even with Adams injured.

items.headline: Corum rushed 17 times for 93 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for eight yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Corum led the Rams in rush attempts and was a close runner-up to Kyren Williams in rushing yards. Corum, like Williams, crossed the goal line as well, recording a four-yard touchdown run with 6:34 remaining in the fourth quarter. Corum's carry and yardage totals were also season highs, but given he'd logged single-digit rush attempts in each of the prior four games, he's more likely than not to continue operating in a clear complementary role behind Williams most weeks.

items.headline: Higbee caught two of three targets for 14 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Higbee was expected to have a chance to see an increase in production with wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) unavailable, but the tight end put together a disappointing performance. Fellow tight ends Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had more impressive days, and it may be hard to predict which of the three will be the go-to option any given week until Terrance Ferguson (ankle) returns from injured reserve.

items.headline: Mumpfield caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win at Las Vegas.
items.summary: With Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua dealing with a calf injury going into game day, it looked like Mumpfield was going to see his role expand in Week 7. While he was second on the team in snaps (28) at wide receiver Sunday, Mumpfield still lagged far behind Nacua (58). As long as the latter remains available, Mumpfield appears unlikely to draw more than a few targets in any given game.

items.headline: Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Parkinson has been banged up seemingly all season, first dealing with shoulder and knee injuries before a ribs issue this week. Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen would be set to handle most of the tight-end duties for the Rams if Parkinson is unable to play, and rookie Max Klare could even see some action on offense.

items.headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: The first-round rookie will not enter Sunday's contest unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Whittington (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Whittington is working through a back issue that flared up during Thursday's practice, and he was held out of Friday's session as a precaution, per Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio. If he's unable to play Sunday, then Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels would all be in line for more offensive snaps. Despite the absence of Davante Adams (hamstring, IR), Whittington was not targeted once during the Rams' Week 7 win over the Raiders.

items.headline: Allen logged six snaps on special teams and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Allen -- who was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins one day after being let go by the Commanders on Oct. 8 -- was cleared to make his debut with his new team Sunday. He was limited to work on special teams, but he could carve himself a role on offense as he gets more familiar with the playbook. Jaylen Wright left Sunday's game and did not return due to a quadriceps injury, and if he cannot play against the Raiders in Week 8, then Allen will step into the RB2 role behind Ollie Gordon.

items.headline: Bell caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
items.summary: The third-round rookie played 31 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. Bell was in on 48 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays and saw the second-most targets behind tight end Greg Dulcich (five).

items.headline: Coleman did not catch his only target in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
items.summary: Coleman played 10 offensive snaps in Sunday's win. The fifth-round rookie participated in just 15 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays, taking a back seat to third-round rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas.

items.headline: Gordon rushed 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown while catching one of three targets for no gain in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Gordon extended his touchdown streak to four games with a one-yard rushing score in the first quarter. Over that four-game span, Gordon has 69 carries for 332 yards and four touchdowns, having established himself as the go-to option in Miami's backfield following De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL tear. If the 1-5 Dolphins can stay competitive at home against the Patriots in Week 8, Gordon would be in line to handle another heavy rushing workload, especially if Jaylen Wright (quadriceps) doesn't play after exiting Sunday's win.

items.headline: Joly (concussion) did not appear on the Dolphins' injury report Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: Joly was inactive for the team's Week 5 loss to the Bengals while recovering from a concussion, but he now appears to be back to full health after Miami's bye week. The tight end will be back in his depth role behind starter Greg Dulcich on Sunday against the Jets.

items.headline: Kacmarek (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday battle against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
items.summary: Kacmarek dealt with a hamstring injury this week and logged limited practices Wednesday and Thursday. However, he was able to upgrade to a full session Friday and has thus been cleared to play Sunday. Kacmarek should serve in his usual role as the No. 2 tight end who focuses primarily on blocking.

items.headline: Washington (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
items.summary: Washington practiced fully Friday after limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. The Dolphins' WR1 in terms of playing time and targets, Washington still hasn't found the end zone this season, producing 26 catches for 289 yards on 39 targets. He's a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy.

items.headline: Wayne (knee) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
items.summary: Wayne was limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but his ability to practice in full Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sundays' AFC East showdown. Wayne made his Dolphins debut against the Jets in Week 7, when he played 16 snaps (10 on offense, six on special teams) without showing up in the box score otherwise.

items.headline: Wright (quadriceps/foot) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Wright exited Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets late in the fourth quarter on account of the quad issue, but his availability for this weekend's game against the Patriots doesn't look to be in any peril. Since returning to action Week 4 against the Vikings following a one-game absence, Wright has been a clear second fiddle to Ollie Gordon out of the Miami backfield. In his last three appearances, Wright hasn't recorded any receptions and has logged no more than six carries in any contest.

items.headline: Addison caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts. He added three yards on his lone carry.
items.summary: No Viking caught more than four passes on the afternoon, and Justin Jefferson was the only member of the team to see more than five targets, so Addison's poor numbers were more a result of his offense's struggles overall than his own performance. The fourth-year wideout still has only one big game in his five appearances so far, with 90 of his 183 receiving yards and his only TD coming Week 3 against Tampa Bay. Addison will try to break out in Week 8 against a struggling Lions secondary.

items.headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is listed as inactive but will serve as the Vikings' third quarterback for Sunday's games versus the Colts.
items.summary: Brosmer remains the emergency reserve quarterback behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. Brosmer will only enter the game if both Murray and Wentz must depart due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Claiborne (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.summary: Claiborne is a healthy scratch for Week 7 due to the return of Jordan Mason, who's been activated from injured reserve after completing his recovery from a thumb injury. Clairborne may have an uphill battle for active status moving forward as long as both Jones and Mason are available.

items.headline: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
items.summary: The veteran tight end scored Minnesota's only TD of the afternoon, connecting with Kyler Murray on a five-yard score early in the fourth quarter. Hockenson has seen more than five targets just once in six contests this season, and he'll take a 27-237-2 line on 32 targets into a potential revenge game in Week 8 against the Lions.

items.headline: Jennings caught two of three targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
items.summary: The veteran wideout entered Week 7 with just two catches for nine yards across four games, so this counts as a breakout game for Jennings. He's running plenty of routes alongside Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison at receiver, but Jennings is deep down the list for targets in Minnesota. He's not a recommended fantasy play for next Sunday against the Lions' leaky secondary.

items.headline: Price (head) was back on the field for the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Colts, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
items.summary: Price was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion, but he's been cleared to return to Sunday's contest. He'll see most of his playing time as a returner on special teams while operating in a rotational role on offense.

items.headline: The Vikings placed Briscoe (undisclosed) on their practice squad injured list Wednesday.
items.summary: It's not immediately clear exactly what happened, but as a result of the move, Briscoe will not be eligible for elevation to the active roster for Minnesota's next four games. He's still waiting to make his regular-season debut since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in May.

items.headline: Minnesota signed Culp to its practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Just a little more than a week after getting cut from the Browns' practice squad, Culp has now found another opportunity with a new club. He suited up for 13 games with the Buccaneers in 2025, catching his only target for six yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Dallas reverted to the Vikings' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Dallas was elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts, but he didn't record any stats while playing six snaps on offense and 13 snaps with the special-teams unit. Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones (knee) handled all the touches in the backfield in the victory. The running back is eligible to be elevated two more times before Minnesota would have to sign him to the active roster, and there appears to be a likelihood one of those promotions could happen in Week 8 since Jones is currently viewed as day-to-day.

items.headline: Minnesota signed Nesbit (undisclosed) to its practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The Vikings waived Nesbit from their injured reserve list with an injury settlement back in August, but he's now back in the building following Week 7. Minnesota also signed tight end Devin Culp to its practice squad Wednesday.

items.headline: Chism caught his sole target for 16 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
items.summary: Chism saw the third most offensive snaps at wide receiver for the Patriots behind A.J. Brown's 49 and DeMario Douglas' 35. The 24-year-old was not given as much attention as in the prior two weeks, with his target share dropping from four targets in Week 5 and six targets in Week 6 to just one in Week 7.

items.headline: Douglas caught three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
items.summary: Douglas played 35 of the Patriots' 54 offensive snaps in the contest and did not find the end zone. The wide receiver had logged three touchdowns in the prior two contests but has now returned to a role with lower priority as A.J. Brown becomes reacquainted with the offense.

items.headline: Kiner rushed four times for 13 yards in Thursday's Week 7 loss to Chicago. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
items.summary: Kiner came into Thursday having gained 50-plus rushing yards in consecutive contests, but he was much less impactful versus the Bears. Part of that was due to New England playing from behind and tallying just 17 total carries as a team (to 31 pass attempts), but it's also notable that Kiner logged just six offensive snaps, well behind Rhamondre Stevenson's 37 and less than half of TreyVeon Henderson's 13. While Kiner's previous two performances gave him a little momentum in fantasy, he's unlikely to be a reliable asset while Stevenson and Henderson are healthy.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive and designated as New England's emergency third quarterback for Thursday's matchup versus Chicago.
items.summary: This has become the routine for Morton, who has worked as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback every week so far this season. The role has yet to land the rookie QB any game reps, and he'll be eligible to enter Thursday's contest only if both quarterbacks ahead of him (Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito) are forced to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Raridon caught three of four targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's Week 7 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Raridon got open late in the third quarter and hauled in a nicely placed pass from Drake Maye for a 30-yard score. The rookie tight end finished third on the team with 56 receiving yards and tied for third with three receptions. Raridon is clearly behind Hunter Henry, who posted a 7-71-0 receiving line on seven targets, in the tight-end pecking order, but he's shown promise early in his career with 12 catches on 16 targets for 168 yards and two TDs through six games.

items.headline: Williams returned two kickoffs for 47 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
items.summary: It was the second game in a row in which Williams saw one target from Drake Maye, and the second-year pro's 21 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Patriots wide receivers. He's been surpassed by Efton Chism in the passing game, and with A.J. Brown back in the mix, it seems like most of Williams' impact moving forward will be on kickoffs as a returner. His playing time will take an even greater hit upon the returns of Mack Hollins (calf) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) from injured reserve. The Patriots will stay on the road for Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: The Patriots signed Miller to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Dolphins waived Miller on Oct. 13 after the wide receiver appeared in all five regular-season games to start 2026. The 26-year-old caught three of his four targets for 92 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots are currently without Mack Hollins (calf) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder), leaving Miller as one of the most likely candidates to be elevated from the practice squad on a week-to-week basis.

items.headline: Brown hauled in all three targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass catcher moving forward.

items.headline: Donaldson (shoulder) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris, Jeff Nowak of The Big 870 New Orleans reports.
items.summary: Donaldson sustained a shoulder injury during the first quarter of Sunday's game, and the injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of the contest. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller will be the Saints' two remaining running backs the rest of the way in Donaldson's absence.

items.headline: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.
items.summary: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

items.headline: Johnson caught one of three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

items.headline: Kamara carried the ball six times for five yards and caught all seven of his targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: The Saints' ground game was completely shut down, as quarterback Tyler Shough led the team with a mere seven rushing yards, but Kamara still contributed through the air and led New Orleans in catches while tying Barion Brown for the game high in receiving yards. Since missing the season opener, Kamara has put together 258 scrimmage yards and three total TDs (two rushing, one receiving) over six games, but the backfield could get more crowded after a Week 8 bye if Travis Etienne (hamstring) is cleared to return.

items.headline: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.
items.summary: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone.
